## What We Did

Learned about the United States Census Bureau's data formats and how to access them using the Census API. We also explored the `tidycensus` package in R.

## Key Concepts

ACS: American Community Survey
1-year, 3-year (no longer exists), and 5-year estimates
with tidycensus: get_acs() - get ACS data

MOE: Margin of Error
State -> County -> Tract -> Block Group -> Block Group
Tract: neighborhood approximation; ~5-8k people, boundaries change between censuses (use longitudinal tract IDs to track changes over time)
Block Groups: small neighborhood approx.; high MOE
Block Group: 10-year census only, limited use

GEOID: US Census geographic identifier
ex: 421010001001
42 - state
101 - county
0001 - tract
001 - block group

## Reflection

I learned a lot about the Census API and tidycensus. As someone who has analyzed census data before, it's great to know that there exists an easier method of obtaining the data through a single command. I would like to explore more the ways in which more granular data can be obtained and how to properly analyze it.
